featured_reviews.name: Nikhil Aher
featured_reviews.review_text:
Disappointing First Experience – Poor Packaging and No Response from Zinque Team

As a first-time customer, I was really looking forward to trying Zinque Patisserie, given its premium reputation and pricing. Unfortunately, my experience was disappointing.

My order (#7377) — Raspberry & Dark Chocolate Mini Cake and Strawberry Special Assorted Box — arrived in poor condition. The cakes were toppled and smudged, which completely took away from the presentation and experience I expected from a gourmet patisserie. Despite reaching out via WhatsApp and email the same day, I received no response.

Taste-wise, the desserts didn’t quite justify the price tag either. Having tried places like Bunty Mahajan, House of Amel, and Moa Bakery, I expected better finesse and consistency.

Overall, the quality, handling, and customer response didn’t match the premium image the brand portrays. I hope the team takes this as constructive feedback and improves packaging and service reliability for future orders.

Its a shame on you guys, you haven’t addressed the issue even now and yet replying here to save yourself instead of actually solving this case - Updated 20th nov 2025
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi Nikhil Aher,

This was in Year 2024 December your message has the date too.It’s disheartening to see you putting up a Review after One Year where it had been sorted.Your insights are crucial for us to grow, and we appreciate you sharing them but not after a year and that also again.

Thanks & Regards,
Zinque Patisserie

featured_reviews.name: Ananaya Chopra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tried Zinqué’s bean plum cake (vegan!) this Christmas and it was an absolute hit. The texture was soft, moist, and beautifully balanced — something that’s honestly hard to get right in a vegan bake.

What stood out most was how thoughtfully done it felt, from the richness of the flavours to the overall consistency. It had that comforting, festive indulgence without feeling heavy.

It’s exciting to see a plant-based Christmas cake done so well. Would highly recommend this if you’re looking for a vegan dessert that doesn’t compromise on taste or quality.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi Ananaya Chopra,
It's wonderful to hear that the bean plum cake was a standout during your Christmas celebrations. The balance of flavors and texture is crucial in vegan baking, and it's rewarding to know we hit the mark with this one. Thank you for recommending it to others in search of a delicious plant-based dessert!
Thanks & Regards,
Zinque Patisserie

We ordered their “burn away” cake in Belgian chocolate with ivory cream frosting for my grandmother’s 100th birthday celebration and it was perfect! Delicious as always and even the design was very elegant and perfectly suited the birthday girl. The whipped cream frosting was very fresh and went surprisingly well with the chocolate cake. It enhanced the taste of the chocolate cake.
The concept of “burn away” cake was completely new for most of us so that was very interesting. The party was planned just 2 days prior and vanilla beans were super helpful at creating the design for such a last moment order. All the guests loved the cake and many diet conscious people took second and third helpings- that’s how irresistible their cakes are!

All of their cakes are excellent, super fresh and mouth wateringly delicious! My personal favourites are the Belgian chocolate and also the pineapple fresh cream the best part of which is the extra chunks of pineapple inside the cake layers!

featured_reviews.name: Murtaza Anverali
featured_reviews.review_text:
Deliciae by Bunty Mahajan: Mango Biscoff Cheesecake = Summer in a Slice*

Deliciae never misses with desserts, but the *Mango Biscoff Cheesecake* is next-level indulgence. If you think mango and Biscoff sounds risky, this will convert you.

*Presentation*: It arrives looking like art. A perfect round slice with that golden mango glaze on top, a generous dusting of Biscoff crumbs, and a caramelized Biscoff biscuit perched on the side. The layers are clean and distinct even before the first bite. You can tell it’s been set with care, not rushed.

*Taste & Texture*: This is where it becomes addictive. The base is a thick, buttery Biscoff crust that holds up without crumbling everywhere. It gives you that warm, spiced caramel note in every forkful. The cheesecake layer is insanely smooth and creamy, with a light tang that cuts through the sweetness. Then comes the mango: real Alphonso pulp, not artificial essence. It’s fresh, tropical, and balances the Biscoff beautifully so nothing feels cloying. The top glaze adds a subtle fruity brightness. Together it’s sweet, spiced, tangy, and lush.

*Overall Experience*: Each bite gives you multiple textures. Crumbly base, silky cheesecake, soft mango layer, and that little crunch from Biscoff crumbs on top. It’s rich but not heavy, and somehow feels both decadent and summery at once. Portion size is generous enough to share, though you won’t want to.

*Vibe at Deliciae*: The patisserie itself matches the dessert. Elegant, pastel, with display counters that make you want everything. Staff are super helpful and package it beautifully if you’re taking away. No soggy cheesecake disasters here.

*Verdict*: Mango + Biscoff sounds like a weird collab that should not work, but Deliciae makes it iconic. This cheesecake is indulgent, balanced, and wildly photogenic. Easily one of the best fusion desserts I have had this season.

*Pro tip*: Pair it with their cold coffee. Thank me later.

Already craving my next slice. If you’re a cheesecake or mango person, skip everything else and get this first.

5-Star Review for Deliciae By Bunty Mahajan
Absolutely Divine! The Hazelnut Divine Cake is a Masterpiece ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

I ordered the 1kg Hazelnut Divine Cake from Deliciae By Bunty Mahajan as a special surprise for an amazing female trainer at the gym – a heartfelt thank you for all her motivation and hard work.

From the moment it arrived, it was clear this was no ordinary cake. The presentation was stunning: a glossy chocolate mirror glaze that shone beautifully, elegant swirls of rich chocolate rosettes, scattered roasted hazelnuts for that perfect crunch, and even a personalized plaque that made it feel extra thoughtful.

But the real magic happened when we cut into it – layers of moist vanilla sponge intertwined with generous chocolate ganache and crunchy roasted hazelnuts. Every bite was an explosion of decadent chocolate-hazelnut flavor, perfectly balanced, not overly sweet, and incredibly indulgent. It truly lived up to its “Divine” name!

This cake didn’t just taste extraordinary; it made her day truly special. Her smile and excitement said it all – it was the highlight of the gym ! At around ₹2631, it was worth every single rupee for the premium quality, freshness, and joy it brought.
Deliciae By Bunty Mahajan continues to be Mumbai’s best pâtisserie for a reason – flawless execution, timely delivery, and cakes that are as beautiful as they are delicious.

Highly recommend for any celebration or just to make someone’s day unforgettable. Thank you, team – you’ve gained a loyal customer!

featured_reviews.name: Siddhesh Kotian
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’m extremely disappointed with J Hearsch & Co. in Bandra. Despite being an old and reputed establishment, their quality, service, and overall experience have gone drastically downhill.

To begin with, the staff—especially the owner—were shockingly rude. It’s as if they believe they’re the only bakery that exists just because they’ve been around a while. Sadly, that attitude is exactly why this was my last visit.

Yes, the place has a legacy, but that doesn’t mean you stop upgrading where it matters. Instead of improving service and food quality, they’ve only focused on increasing their prices while everything else has degraded. The quantity has reduced significantly, and the quality is no longer what it used to be.

Here’s what I ordered:
•	Chicken Burger
•	Chicken Samosa
•	Mutton Samosa
•	Mutton Puff
•	Chicken Roll
•	Lime Water

The burger used to come with wafers in a decent box—now it’s wrapped in flimsy paper. The lime water, which once had good quantity for a reasonable price, is now expensive (₹100) and barely enough. Most items were just okay, but not worth the price or the hassle.

There is no seating, no parking, and still, customers are expected to follow a long list of rules. Instead of focusing on unnecessary regulations, they should really work on their customer service, which is currently pathetic.

Honestly, there’s no point in putting in so much effort to visit a place where the staff behaves rudely and the food no longer justifies the hype or price. I won’t be returning, and I certainly won’t recommend this bakery to anyone. Keep your attitude—I’ll take my business elsewhere.

featured_reviews.review_text: Tried the burger at J. Hearsch Bakery – hands down the best I’ve ever had! Loved the twist with mango sauce and real ketchup. The mutton samosa was delicious too, though the wine biscuits were a bit too sweet for our taste. Just one downside – you can’t eat nearby as they don’t allow standing around the area. Still, a must-try spot for some amazing bakery bites! 🍔🥟🍪

featured_reviews.review_text:
This beautiful, quaint and petite cafe ‘Nostalgia’ in Bandra, feels like a warm hug from my childhood. The moment you enter, your eyes start bouncing from one decor to another. Think old films, action figures, whimsical walls, gingham aprons, Christmas figs, and those iconic cutting chai glasses—it's like an Easter egg hunt for the heart, straight from the '90s! Also, the sun shimmers beautifully through the windows, casting playful shadows on the cozy wooden tables.  The food is another thing that seals the deal. Cute little chicken samosas & quiches are just a few of the things that were light yet bursting with flavour. We topped it off with the classic cold coffee, which was made in this cool corner of the cafe, complete with swing doors and retro plastic curtains.

Cafe ‘Nostalgia’ truly lives up to it’s name,
and feels like time travel with good food.

featured_reviews.name: Yaana Dalvi
featured_reviews.review_text: 5/5 stars aren't enough for this gem of a bakery! Tucked away in the heart of Bandra, Nostalgia Old School Bakery is a must-visit destination for anyone with a sweet tooth and a love for nostalgia. As soon as you step inside, you're transported to a bygone era. The bakery's vintage decor, complete with antique baking equipment and retro posters, is an instant mood-booster. The aroma of freshly baked goods wafting from the oven is the perfect accompaniment to the warm and cozy atmosphere. Now, onto the main event – the baked goods! Oh, the sheer variety and quality of the treats on offer is staggering. From classic cakes and pastries to innovative desserts and breads, every item on the menu is a masterclass in texture, flavor, and presentation. But what truly sets Nostalgia apart is the love and care that goes into every single item. You can taste the difference that fresh, high-quality ingredients and meticulous attention to detail make. The service is top-notch, too. The staff are warm, friendly, and happy to help you navigate the menu or customize your order. In short, Nostalgia Old School Bakery is a game-changer. Whether you're a local or just visiting, do yourself a favor and swing by this incredible bakery. Your taste buds will thank you!

featured_reviews.name: Anusuya
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve been visiting American Express Bakery for nearly 30 years now and it continues to feel like stepping into a delicious slice of my own history. What amazes me most is how beautifully they’ve maintained the quality of their food over the decades. It's consistent, comforting and absolutely delightful every single time.

Their Chicken Lorraine remains unbeatable, the Mutton Pattice is still one of the best you’ll find in the city and the Salami Sandwich has that perfect old-school flavour that’s hard to come by anymore. The bread pudding tastes exactly the way it did years ago: warm, nostalgic and wonderfully homely. They also have an excellent range of tea cakes, each one soft, simple and packed with flavour. And of course, the cream rolls. They are light, crisp, perfectly filled...arguably the best in town.

The charm of this place extends far beyond the food. The interiors still hold the magic of an earlier era with wooden shelves, warm lighting and classic glass-fronted cabinets displaying freshly baked goodies, just like in the photos I’ve shared. There’s something incredibly comforting about standing in that space; it feels timeless, familiar and beautifully untouched by passing trends.

American Express Bakery isn’t just a bakery—it’s tradition, nostalgia and consistency wrapped in the aroma of fresh bakes. A true Bandra gem that only gets better with time.

featured_reviews.name: Divya
featured_reviews.review_text:
American Express Bakery in Bandra is one of those “heritage” spots — over 100 years old and super well known. So naturally, we were curious and had decent expectations going in. But honestly? It was pretty average.

We tried a couple of their cheesecakes, brownies and patties — it all tasted just… mid. Nothing bad, but nothing memorable either. The kind of stuff you’d expect at a regular bakery, not one with a century-old reputation.

What also stood out — and not in a good way — was the staff. They came across as a bit rude and uppity, almost like they were doing us a favour by just being there. For a place that sees so much footfall and has that legacy, you’d expect more warmth or at least basic courtesy.

It’s also priced a bit on the higher side, which would be totally fine if the quality matched up — but it really didn’t.

So yeah, for the hype and the history, it fell short. If you’re in the area, maybe check it out once just for the legacy factor. But don’t go in expecting to be blown away.

Note:These are budget-friendly snacks, so don't expect chunks of chicken in every bite, but the flavor is definitely there!
Also don't go by their display , if tray is empty on display they still may have it stored inside .

The staff is friendly and the service is incredibly quick. They bake in batches about three times a day, so if your choice isn't piping hot, just ask them to heat it up for you—they are happy to oblige.

Be prepared to queue up, especially on weekends and in the evenings. Even with a crowd, the line moves fast, so don't let the rush pull you away.

featured_reviews.review_text:

I recently ordered food and spat almost all of it out in utter disgust! Chicken cutlets - no sign of chicken, huge and deceiving packed with filler (maida, cornflour, maybe a dash of potato) with an overpowering taste of cinnamon. Absolutely sickening to be duped this way. Chicken pan rolls, one of their best selling items, had sharp bones in it which could get masked under the crunch of the coating if not chewed carefully. Not to forget the horrid chunks if chewy chicken fat/ maybe the wastes of chicken on second thoughts, interspersed through this seemingly tasty roll. One word - GROSS! Mutton puffs were a saving grace, though dripping in oil, were fairly edible with some sign of meat. Non vegetarians, ditch this place. Vegetarians - if you’re a fan of cornflour and maida filler, this place is a go to!

Never ever eating from this place again!

Best Cakes: -

1. Belgian Chocolate cake: - This is the most selling cake of Le 15 & once you will have it you will know why? Book it for the next special occasion.

Why I love Le 15?
The way Pooja Dhingra has created all the outlets with so much love & the way she has marketed Le 15, I am a fan of her. She is very inspirational, also created the magnum series a few days back.

| Conclusion|

If you are in Bombay rush to the outlet right now and if you are not when you visit, make it a point to visit Le 15.

P.S: -The pictures that you will click at Le 15 will be the gorgeous pictures on your Instagram Feed

featured_reviews.name: Arzan Dumasia
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently had the pleasure of trying out the desserts from Country Of Origin, and I must say, it was quite an experience. I ordered their desserts for delivery at home, and they did not disappoint.

1. Salted Caramel and Chocolate Mousse (Very Good):
The first dessert I tried was the Salted Caramel and Chocolate Mousse, and it was an absolute delight. The dessert featured a thick, buttery caramel sauce with a subtle hint of sea salt, perfectly sandwiched between Country Of Origin's luxurious chocolate mousse. The combination of sweet and salty flavors was on point, and the texture was incredibly smooth and creamy. It left a wonderful lingering taste on my palate, making it a standout dish.

2. Turkish Coffee Dark Chocolate Mousse (Very Good):
The Turkish Coffee Dark Chocolate Mousse was another winner. This dessert showcased Country Of Origin's signature dark chocolate mousse infused with the earthy and robust flavor of Turkish coffee. The result was a rich and decadent treat with a bittersweet taste that was simply heavenly. I appreciated the collaboration with Mediterranea, as it added a unique twist to this dessert.

3. Eggless Dark Chocolate Chunk Cookie (OK):
Moving on to the Eggless Dark Chocolate Chunk Cookie, I have to admit that it didn't quite live up to the high standard set by the previous desserts. While it was good, it fell into the "okay" category for me. The cookie had a nice, deep chocolate flavor, and the chunks of dark chocolate were a definite plus. However, it lacked that soft, gooey texture that makes cookies truly exceptional.

4. Eggless Caramelized Cashew Nuts (OK):
Similarly, the Eggless Caramelized Cashew Nuts were also in the "okay" range. These nuts had a good caramelized sweetness to them, but they didn't stand out as much as the mousse desserts did. They provided a nice crunch, but I was hoping for a bit more of a caramelized punch in the flavour.

In conclusion, Country Of Origin's desserts truly shine in the mousse category. The Salted Caramel and Chocolate Mousse and the Turkish Coffee Dark Chocolate Mousse were exceptional, offering a symphony of flavors and textures that left me craving more. While the cookies and caramelized cashew nuts were decent, they didn't quite reach the same level of excellence. I would highly recommend trying out the mousse desserts if you have the chance, whether dining in at the restaurant or ordering them for delivery – they are a sweet indulgence worth savoring.
